Definition of done:
- API tokens are generated as `tly_` plus 40 random `[A-Za-z0-9]` characters, and only the SHA-256 hex hash and last four characters are stored. The full token is returned once, by create and invite-accept, and nowhere else.
- Auth hashes the presented token, and old plain-text snapshot tokens still load and authenticate. The next snapshot written contains no plain-text token. Revoked keys and removed members still get 401.

API keys are now stored as a SHA-256 hash plus last four characters, and the full token leaves the server only in the create and invite-accept answers.

**Files changed**
- `internal/store/store.go`: the new token generator (`newAPIKeyToken`, rejection sampling so every character is equally likely), `hashToken`, `last4`, and a hash index in place of the token index. `APIKeyByToken` hashes the presented token. `TouchAPIKey` skips a write when the recorded use is under 60 seconds old.
- `internal/store/types.go`: `APIKey` gains `Hash` and `Last4`. `Token` is now `omitempty` and is set only on the value returned by create.
- `internal/store/state.go`: `FromState` hashes any legacy plain-text token, keeps the key, and clears the token. Snapshot v1 loads go through the same path.
- `internal/api/team.go`: list and create responses go through explicit views (`apiKeyView`, `createdAPIKey`). The list never carries a token or hash. Create and invite-accept carry `token`.
- `cmd/tally/main.go`: the demo seed used to log the full token. It now logs the key ID and last4, and prints the token once to stdout.
- Tests: `store_test.go`, `snapshot_test.go`, `api_test.go`.

- The list views keep `org_id`, since existing clients may read it. The spec's field list didn't mention it.

The change meets the task. I found no correctness, security or requirement problems.

- **Generation and storage:** `newAPIKeyToken` produces `tly_` plus 40 characters from `[A-Za-z0-9]` using `crypto/rand`, with rejection of bytes ≥248 so the modulo is unbiased. `createAPIKey` stores only the SHA-256 hex hash and last four characters. The map value never holds the token, so `Export` and snapshots cannot contain it.
- **Full token returned once:** `POST /v1/api-keys` and `POST /v1/invites/accept` return the token through `createdAPIKeyView`. `GET /v1/api-keys` uses `viewAPIKey`, which has no `token` or `hash` field. No other handler serialises `store.APIKey` directly.
- **Auth:** `APIKeyByToken` hashes the presented token and looks it up in `keysByHash`. Revoked keys and removed members still return 401 through the unchanged checks in `authed`.
- **Legacy snapshots:** `FromState` hashes any plain-text `Token`, sets `Last4`, clears `Token`, and indexes by hash. v1 snapshots pass through `migrateV1` into the same path. The next `Save` writes no plain-text token, and the tests cover both cases.
- **Throttle:** `TouchAPIKey` skips the write when the last recorded use is under 60 seconds old. The boundary (59s skipped, 60s recorded) is tested.
- **Logs:** the seed command now logs the key ID and last four characters, not the token. It prints the token once to stdout, labelled as shown once.

Optional notes, not reasons to revise:
- `TouchAPIKey` with a `now` earlier than the recorded use (clock moved backwards) leaves `last_used_at` unchanged. That is safe, but it may hold a future timestamp until the clock catches up.
- The seed command's stdout line is the one place a token is printed outside the create answers. It is a CLI demo output, so I'd accept it as is.
